approachQuestion.prompt:
Closest times on a circular dial

Times are minute marks on a 24-hour circular dial, represented by integers from 0 through 1439. Return the smallest elapsed separation in minutes between any two distinct entries, allowing the interval that crosses midnight. Duplicate marks are allowed. The input may be reordered.

Constraints: 2 ≤ n ≤ 200,000.

Examples: [2,1438,700] → 4. [100,100] → 0.

Choose a valid method that meets the full contract with the least unnecessary work.
constraints: The stated input/output and mutation requirements apply to every option.

options.text: Sort the marks, find the smallest adjacent difference, and also compare the first and last marks across midnight using 1440−last+first.
options.feedback: On a circle the closest pair is adjacent in sorted order or is the wraparound pair.

options.text: Compare only adjacent marks after sorting.
options.feedback: [2,1438] has circular separation 4, which the ordinary gap misses.

options.text: Return the difference between the largest and smallest mark.
options.feedback: This ignores the shorter midnight arc; [2,1438] gives ordinary gap 1436 but circular gap 4.

options.text: Compare every unordered pair using the shorter of its two circular distances.
options.feedback: This is correct for all inputs, but checking every pair repeats work avoided by sorted neighbors.

feedback.reason: The smallest circular separation may cross midnight.
details: Comparison-sort the marks, scan consecutive gaps, and evaluate the wrap gap 1440−last+first; return the smallest.
The smallest circular separation may cross midnight. Compare ordinary adjacent gaps and the wrap gap 1440-last+first; scanning only consecutive sorted marks misses the first/last pair.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed revealed method, choose its tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space bounds. Count copies, sorting buffer and recursion stack; exclude caller input and returned output. Comparison merge sort uses a linear buffer; comparisons and moves are constant-time.

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(n) additional space

feedback.reason: Sort marks and include the single wraparound gap in the scan.
details: Comparison merge sort takes O(n log n) worst-case time; its copied records and merge buffer require O(n) auxiliary space. The recursion stack is O(log n), within O(n). Linear time omits sorting, quadratic time overstates the sort cost; constant space omits the buffer.
